title: Serialize & Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Pre-order DFS with null markers makes serialization round-trippable: serialize emits a comma-separated stream, deserialize consumes it via a shared queue/index.

notes: Pre-order alone is ambiguous — you need explicit null markers (or BOTH pre + in-order) to recover the shape.
Deserialize must consume tokens IN ORDER via a shared index or shifted queue; recursing without state corrupts the stream.
Use String(val) on write and Number(tok) on read — splitting on comma turns numbers into strings.

questions.q: Why does pre-order with null markers uniquely identify a binary tree?
options: Null markers record the absence of children, so the shape is reconstructable
Because all binary trees are unique by their values
Because the root is always first

questions.q: What state must deserialize share across recursive calls?
options: A position/index (or queue) into the token stream

questions.q: Time complexity of serialize on n nodes?
Why convert tokens with Number() during deserialize?
options: split(",") yields strings; the val field should be numeric
questions.explain: Splitting on a comma gives string tokens. Without Number(), node.val would be the string "3", not 3.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the pre-order serialize/deserialize with `#` null markers.

L3.prompt: Implement serialize(root) and deserialize(s) using pre-order DFS with `#` null markers. Build a sample tree [1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5], round-trip it via serialize(deserialize(serialize(root))), and log the result.
hints: Pre-order: write self, recurse left, recurse right. Write `#` for null.
Deserialize shares an index `i` across recursive calls — every call consumes exactly one token, then recurses for its two children.
